Subject: Performance SLO recap + next steps (latency, concurrency, streaming)

Thanks for the call this morning — great conversation and clear priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary of targets you shared:
- P95 latency (end-to-end generation) target: 300 ms for initial token start when streaming is enabled; overall P95 for full 512-token responses ~450 ms (goal).
- Steady-state throughput: avg ~200 qps, peak concurrency up to ~50 concurrent requests (spiky retail traffic).
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for perceived latency (fast first token).
- Quality: prefer the base 13B family for accuracy, but open to exploring a 7B variant for cost-sensitive endpoints.

Immediate asks / next steps from Redwood:
1) Provide a short digest of cost/performance levers that will let you hit the P95 targets while controlling unit cost (continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile, model variants).
2) Quick sizing + cost estimate (1M tokens / month baseline and a peak-day estimate) — we’ll include conservative and optimistic configurations.
3) Meet again next week for an ops walkthrough (30 min) to review config and any infra constraints (KMS, VPC).

I’m attaching a concise doc with recommended levers and a quick sizing sheet (short PDF + spreadsheet) — delivering now; Rishi will follow up with more technical notes.

Best,

- The 300 ms P95 is the most important SLA for customer-facing search results (we measure time-to-first-token, so streaming start is critical).

Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap + next steps (latency, concurrency, streaming)

Adding technical notes and quick recommendations to hit the time-to-first-token P95 and control cost. High level first, then config bullets: 

High-level approach:
- Prioritize time-to-first-token: enable streaming with aggressive kernel warmup and small initial batch timeouts (to avoid waiting for large batches for the first token).
- Use continuous batching for throughput efficiency, but with dynamic batch timeouts to preserve tail latency during spikes.
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts and deterministic system prefixes (search context), which reduces compute for many queries.
- Quantize to 4-bit (QLoRA-style or runtime 4-bit kernels) for 13B to reduce memory and improve throughput with small accuracy tradeoffs; keep a 13B FP16 fallback for high-accuracy routes.

Concrete levers and suggested params:
- Continuous batching: target nominal batch size 32 for steady-state; dynamic timeout 6-8 ms to favor low latency and let batches accumulate when load is high. Increase nominal batch size to 64 for cheaper throughput during predicted non-interactive windows.
- Streaming config: prioritize first-token generation by allowing a short micro-batch (batch-size 1-4) and pre-warm KV cache for repeated users. This typically brings time-to-first-token down ~40-60% vs naive batching.
- Caching: enable prefix caching for the top 40% of  queries (heuristic based on your logs). TTL: 5 minutes for session-level caches, longer for static prefixes.
- Quantization profile: 4-bit asymmetric quantization for the 13B model on A100/H100-equivalent hardware; expect ~2.5-3x throughput improvement vs FP16 in many common kernels. Maintain a FP16 variant for the highest-quality route (can be used for canary/QA).
- Model variants/routing: route 80% of production search queries to quantized 13B with streaming; route heuristics like autocomplete/suggestions to a 7B quantized model for ~3x lower cost. Use per-route fallback to FP16 if quality drops in evals.

Estimated cost / rough numbers (very rough, will refine in sheet):
- Config A (latency-first): Quantized 13B + streaming + caching, continuous batching tuned for low timeout: ~ $1,100 per 1M tokens.
- Config B (cost-balanced): 13B quantized with more aggressive caching + 7B routing for low-value queries: ~ $650 per 1M tokens.
- Config C (quality-first, FP16 fallback): Mix of FP16 13B for 25% of traffic and quantized 13B for rest: ~ $1,800 per 1M tokens.

Ops considerations / questions for Nova Retail:
- Can you share a sample of traffic distribution (percent interactive vs. async, token length distribution)? That will let us refine batch sizing and cost.
- Any constraints around KMS/VPC or external network that would affect model cold-start times?

Next steps I recommend:
1) I’ll upload a short PDF with the bullets above + a one-sheet cost table (attached).
2) Marissa to send proposed Tue 10:00am PT meeting — I’ll join to walk through ops details and sizing.
3) If you can share a day's trace or token histogram, we’ll produce a tighter estimate.

-Rishi
